# Home solar units model

*Generated by `python -m solvia.pipeline --steps model_pv_home`.*

kWh = kWp × sunlight × other losses × (1 + γ (T_cell − 25 °C)); T_cell from the day's sunlight and max / min air temperature.

| Parameter | Value | From |
|---|---|---|
| k, module heating | 26.9 °C per kW/m² (R² 0.872) | Kaggle plants, 24 train days |
| a, air temperature while sunny | T_min + 0.72 × (T_max − T_min) | same |
| b, sunlight-weighted irradiance | 0.113 kW/m² per kWh/m²/day | same |
| γ, temperature coefficient | -0.4 % per °C | crystalline-silicon datasheet value |
| other losses | 0.86 | assumption: inverter, wiring, dust, mismatch |

## Daily check on the 5 validation days (per-inverter scale fitted on train days)

| Model | Daily error | MAE per inverter-day |
|---|---|---|
| no temperature effect | 5.63 % | 353.0 kWh |
| datasheet gamma | 4.05 % | 269.9 kWh |

The plants' 5 test days are not used. Limits: utility plants, May–June only (26–39 °C), plane-of-array sunlight; homes use NASA POWER horizontal sunlight, so the tilt gain is not modelled. A user calibration (units on a clear sunny day) corrects the overall level.
